order_note: No predecessor. SQL 167 adds one SECURITY DEFINER function and replaces nothing (owner 2026-11-14: "Need to be able to change/correct claim number once edited for ledger to link to existing claim"; decisions: before deposit only, the check's loss draft file and signature requests move with it, a number that matches no claim keeps today's rename): claim_ledger_relink_check(uuid, uuid, text, text, uuid), action inspect or relink, locks the check, refuses tenant_mismatch, a deposited, voided or returned check (SQL 43's rule) and an unlinked one (SQL 44's job), finds the claim with SQL 44's same-tenant match copied exactly (ambiguous, cross_tenant, no_match; never creates, renames or deletes a claim), and on relink moves the check's claim_id (guarded on the claim it read), this check's loss_draft_tracking and signature_requests rows still on the old claim, and writes one check_audit_log row (claim_relinked); never another check, claim_settlements, payouts or either claims row. EXECUTE checksops and the owner only. The spec prerequisites are the file's own (55000 sql167_prerequisite_missing), SQL 41's ocr_claim_number_key(text) among them; the applying login must reach check_intake_items, claims, loss_draft_tracking, signature_requests, check_audit_log and claim_settlements as the definer past RLS (definer_can_write_relations; the file refuses otherwise, sql167_definer_cannot_reach). No table, column, policy, table grant, trigger or row changes, so the db-readonly-validate trigger count is not affected. Expected pre-state in both environments: the function absent (release sql167 v1: 45b7f3a90b7613a53af9e72b569d59f16cdb0de40119ecd6fbe6f2213ea19343, releaseStateHash('sql167', {})). The API (claim_ledger_relink_check in the RPC route) and the Review screen ship after this through their own guarded paths; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.
